Edelbaum's law is a closed-form circle-to-circle combined plane-change steering law for a planetocentric low-thrust spiral. Applied to a heliocentric transfer it is not a weak baseline, it is the wrong equation, and a broken baseline inflates every RL win measured against it.

A Kilopower-class NEP stage is ~10 kWe, roughly 0.4 N of thrust. A crewed fast-transfer stack is >=50 t, so acceleration is ~8e-6 m/s^2 and the transfer is a multi-year spiral against a mission defined by a <=180-day constraint. Every seed fails for the same trivial reason, which is not a measurement of the controller.
